findings.commitment: Real-time wallet screening for Tron payouts

promise_quotes.quote: NUSD payouts that Atlas routes over Tron will also have the receiving wallet screened in real time before funds are released, so your Indonesian partners are covered from day one.

findings.reason: Tron is not a network supported by the on-chain wallet screening catalogue entry for Singapore, so real-time Tron wallet screening cannot be delivered even with an approved exception.

findings.commitment: Real-time wallet screening for Tron payouts

promise_quotes.quote: NUSD payouts that Atlas routes over Tron will also have the receiving wallet screened in real time before funds are released, so your Indonesian partners are covered from day one.

findings.reason: The proposal's Tron wallet-screening commitment is not reflected anywhere in the SOW, Annex 1 or the Agreement, and nothing withdraws it.

findings.commitment: Sanctions and name screening capacity promised at up to 60,000 checks a day

promise_quotes.quote: Name and sanctions screening is sized at up to sixty thousand checks a day, comfortably above your forecast peak.

contract_quote.quote: Elva will screen customer and beneficiary names against sanctions lists at volumes of up to 30,000 screenings per day.

findings.subject: sanctions
findings.reason: The proposal promises sanctions screening capacity of up to 60,000 checks a day, but the SOW caps the same service at 30,000 per day, a direct sizing conflict that undercuts the customer's peak-volume forecast.

findings.commitment: Payout ledger connector provisioned for 30,000 payouts per day

promise_quotes.quote: The payout ledger connector will be provisioned for 30,000 payouts daily from launch.

note_quote.quote: Proposal sizing is 30,000/day. No approval on file for volume above the limit.

findings.reason: The promised 30,000 payouts per day exceeds the Singapore catalogue limit of 25,000 for the payout ledger connector, and no approved exception has been recorded.

findings.commitment: Ingest third-party behavioural/device risk scores into fraud rules and investigations from go-live

promise_quotes.quote: Elva will ingest the device and behavioural risk scores from your existing behavioural-biometrics vendor and make them available to fraud rules and investigators from go-live.

note_quote.quote: Exception approved in principle on deal desk call, 17 Oct. Approver: not recorded.

findings.reason: The third-party behavioural intelligence connector requires a named approval for Singapore, but the pricing note only records an approval in principle with no named approver, so it is not properly authorised to sell.

findings.commitment: Ingest third-party behavioural/device risk scores into fraud rules and investigations from go-live

promise_quotes.quote: Elva will ingest the device and behavioural risk scores from your existing behavioural-biometrics vendor and make them available to fraud rules and investigators from go-live.

findings.reason: The commitment to ingest behavioural/device risk scores from the customer's biometrics vendor is absent from the SOW and Agreement, and nothing withdraws it, despite the customer's fraud-rule build depending on it.

findings.commitment: Automatic drafting of suspicious transaction reports from the case record

promise_quotes.quote: Suspicious transaction reports will be drafted automatically from the case record, ready for your MLRO to review and file.
Once an analyst marks a case as suspicious, we generate the STR for them.

findings.reason: The automatic STR-drafting commitment that the customer's MLRO team is relying on does not appear anywhere in the SOW or Agreement, and nothing withdraws it.
